title: Following written directions
blurb: Follow practical directions exactly: the next step, the skipped step, the right branch of an 'if' and the words except, unless and only if.
question: A medication leaflet says: 'If you miss a dose, take it when you remember, unless your next dose is due within 4 hours; in that case, skip the missed dose.' A patient remembers at 6:00 p.m. and is due again at 8:00 p.m. What should the patient do, and which words in the directions decide it?

teach.h: Directions mean exactly what they say
teach.body: Formally, comprehending written directions means carrying out multi-step instructions exactly and in order, applying each step to the result of the step before, and following any conditions as written. In plain English: do what the page says, not what seems sensible, and do it in the order it says. TEAS items ask for the next step, a skipped step, what to do under a stated condition, or the final outcome.

1. Tap 'Check In' on the welcome screen.
2. Enter your date of birth.
3. If your name appears, tap 'Confirm'. If it does not, tap 'Help' and wait for a staff member.
4. Scan your insurance card unless you are paying for the visit yourself.
5. Take the printed ticket and wait until your number appears on the screen.

teach.caption: Decide which branch fits the person in the question before choosing a 'next step'.

head: Word
What it means for the step
rows: Do it, but not when the condition is true
Every item but the one named
Do it when the condition is true, never otherwise
Fixes the order, whatever order it is written in

items: Read every step before acting: a later step can change an earlier one ('Before step 2, ...').
Underline condition words: if, otherwise, unless, except, only if, before, after.
Decide which branch applies to the person in the question.
Apply each step to the result of the previous step, not the starting point.
Reread the question: next step, skipped step or final outcome?

teach.body: 'Unless' means 'if not': 'Scan your card unless you are paying yourself' means a self-paying patient skips the scan. 'Except' carves out one item: 'Complete every section except D' means D stays blank. 'Only if' sets a requirement: 'Sign Section E only if you are a guardian' means an adult patient signing for herself leaves E blank. Boundary words matter too: 'longer than three days' does not include exactly three.

teach.text: The classic errors: skipping or reordering a step; following the wrong branch of an 'if'; ignoring an except or unless; misreading a boundary ('more than 3' excludes 3); and choosing what seems sensible rather than what the directions say. An option that is a correct step but not the NEXT step is the most common trap.

teach.h: Scenario: Luis and the missed dose
teach.body: Luis Ortega's leaflet says to take a missed dose when he remembers, unless the next dose is due within 4 hours, in which case he skips it. He remembers at 6:00 p.m. and is due again at 8:00 p.m. That is 2 hours, which is within 4, so the 'unless' applies: he skips the missed dose and takes his regular dose at 8:00 p.m. Taking it 'to be safe' would ignore the directions.

items: Read all the directions first, then follow them exactly and in order.
Pick the branch of each 'if' that fits the person in the question.
Unless = if not; except = all but; only if = required condition.
The most common wrong answer is a real step that is not the next one.

summary: You can now follow practical written directions exactly: choosing the next step, spotting a skipped step and taking the correct branch of a condition. You can also handle unless, except, only if and boundary wording without slipping.

A.q:
Read the directions.

Rapid test kit
1. Wash and dry your hands.
2. Open the pouch and place the test card on a flat surface.
3. Add 3 drops of buffer to the sample well.
4. Wait 15 minutes, then read the result.
5. Do not read the result after 20 minutes have passed; the reading will not be valid.

Counting from when the buffer was added, at which of these times can the result be read validly?
options: 10 minutes
14 minutes
17 minutes
22 minutes
A.why: The result is read after waiting 15 minutes and is no longer valid after 20 minutes, so the window is 15 to 20 minutes. Only 17 minutes falls inside it.

whyNot.0: At 10 minutes, the 15-minute wait in step 4 is not finished.
whyNot.1: At 14 minutes, the wait is still one minute short.
whyNot.3: Step 5 says a reading after 20 minutes is not valid.

A.q:
Read the directions.

Time-off requests
1. Log in to the staff portal.
2. Select 'Requests', then 'Time Off'.
3. Enter the dates you are requesting.
4. Attach a coverage form if the request is longer than three days.
5. Click 'Submit' and save the confirmation number.

Jada is requesting Wednesday, Thursday and Friday off. Which of the following does the procedure require her to do?
options: Attach a coverage form before clicking 'Submit'
Submit the request without a coverage form
Enter her dates after she clicks 'Submit'
Ask a supervisor to sign the coverage form
A.why: Wednesday to Friday is three days. A coverage form is needed only when the request is longer than three days, so Jada submits without one.

whyNot.0: Boundary error: exactly three days is not longer than three days.
whyNot.2: Reorders the steps: dates are entered in step 3, before submitting in step 5.
whyNot.3: No supervisor signature appears anywhere in the directions.

A.q:
Read the notice.

Visitor parking: Visitors must park in Lot C. Lot A is for staff, except that visitors displaying a disability placard may also park there. Lot B is closed for repaving.

Ms. Ruiz is a visitor with a disability placard. Where may she park?
options: Lot A, but not Lot C
Lot C, but not Lot A
Lot A or Lot C
Lot B or Lot C
A.why: All visitors may use Lot C, and the exception lets placard holders 'also' use Lot A. So Ms. Ruiz may use either Lot A or Lot C.

whyNot.0: 'Also' adds Lot A; it does not take Lot C away from placard holders.
whyNot.1: This ignores the exception that opens Lot A to visitors with a placard.
whyNot.3: Lot B is closed for repaving.

B.q:
Read the directions.

Visitor badge kiosk
1. Scan your photo ID.
2. If you are visiting a patient, enter the patient's room number. If you are attending a meeting, enter your host's last name.
3. Look at the camera for your photo.
4. Take your printed badge and wear it above the waist.

Ben is attending a meeting with Dr. Hale. He has just scanned his ID. What should he do next?
options: Enter the room number of Dr. Hale's office
Look at the camera to have his photo taken
Enter Dr. Hale's last name at the kiosk
Take his badge and wear it above his waist
B.why: After step 1, Ben reaches the fork in step 2. He is attending a meeting, so he enters his host's last name.

whyNot.0: Room numbers are for people visiting a patient, the other branch of step 2.
whyNot.1: This is step 3; it skips step 2.
whyNot.3: This is step 4, the final step.

B.q:
Read the leaflet.

Take 1 tablet every 8 hours. Do not take more than 3 tablets in 24 hours. If you miss a dose, take it when you remember, unless your next dose is due within 2 hours. In that case, skip the missed dose.

Luis takes his tablets at 6:00 a.m., 2:00 p.m. and 10:00 p.m. One day he forgets his 6:00 a.m. dose and remembers it at 12:30 p.m. What should he do?
options: Take a tablet now and push his next dose to 8:30 p.m.
Take two tablets at 2:00 p.m. to make up for the dose
Take a tablet now and his next tablet at 2:00 p.m.
Skip the missed dose and take a tablet at 2:00 p.m.
B.why: From 12:30 p.m. to 2:00 p.m. is 1 hour 30 minutes, which is within 2 hours. The 'unless' condition applies, so he skips the missed dose and takes his regular one at 2:00 p.m.

whyNot.0: The 'unless' condition applies, so he should not take the missed dose, and the leaflet never says to shift the schedule.
whyNot.1: The leaflet says to skip the missed dose, not double the next one.
whyNot.2: Taking a tablet now ignores the 'unless' condition, because his next dose is due within 2 hours.

B.q:
Read the directions.

The form has Sections A through E. Complete every section except Section D, which is for office use. Sign Section E only if you are the patient's legal guardian. Return the form to the front desk.

Kim, an adult, is completing the form for her own appointment. Which sections should she fill in?
options: Sections A, B, C and E
Sections A, B, C and D
Sections A through E
Sections A, B and C
B.why: Section D is excluded for everyone ('except Section D'). Section E applies only to legal guardians, and Kim is the patient herself, so she completes A, B and C.

whyNot.0: Section E is signed only by a legal guardian; Kim is the patient.
whyNot.1: Section D is for office use, the exception named in the directions.
whyNot.2: This ignores both the exception for D and the condition on E.

C.q:
Read the procedure.

Routine specimens collected before 3:00 p.m. go in the blue bin. Routine specimens collected at or after 3:00 p.m. go in the refrigerator. Specimens labeled STAT go straight to the lab window, whatever time they were collected.

Which specimen was handled correctly?
options: A routine specimen collected at 3:00 p.m., put in the blue bin
A STAT specimen collected at 10:00 a.m., put in the blue bin
A routine specimen collected at 2:45 p.m., put in the refrigerator
A STAT specimen collected at 3:30 p.m., taken to the lab window
C.why: STAT specimens always go to the lab window, whatever the collection time, so the 3:30 p.m. STAT specimen was handled correctly.

whyNot.0: Boundary error: 'at or after 3:00 p.m.' includes 3:00, so this specimen belongs in the refrigerator.
whyNot.1: STAT specimens go to the lab window, not the blue bin, even in the morning.
whyNot.2: 2:45 p.m. is before 3:00 p.m., so this routine specimen belongs in the blue bin.

C.q:
Read the directions.

Home blood pressure monitor: Insert the batteries before you plug in the monitor. Once it is plugged in, sit quietly for five minutes. When the five minutes are up, wrap the cuff around your upper arm. Do not press START until the cuff is in place.

In which order should the actions be done?
options: Plug in, insert batteries, sit, wrap cuff, press START
Insert batteries, plug in, sit, wrap cuff, press START
Insert batteries, plug in, wrap cuff, sit, press START
Insert batteries, sit, plug in, wrap cuff, press START
C.why: Batteries come before plugging in; sitting comes once it is plugged in; the cuff goes on when the five minutes are up; START comes after the cuff is in place.

whyNot.0: The directions say to insert the batteries before plugging in.
whyNot.2: The cuff is wrapped when the five minutes of sitting are up, not before.
whyNot.3: Sitting begins once the monitor is plugged in, so plugging in comes first.

C.q:
Read the procedure.

At the start of each shift, check the glove supply in every exam room. Rooms with exactly one box get one new box. Rooms with no boxes get two new boxes. Record each room you restock in the supply log.

At the start of a shift, Room 1 has 3 boxes, Room 2 has 1 box, Room 3 has no boxes and Room 4 has 2 boxes. Which result follows the procedure?
options: 3 new boxes; 2 rooms recorded in the log
2 new boxes; 2 rooms recorded in the log
3 new boxes; 4 rooms recorded in the log
4 new boxes; 3 rooms recorded in the log
C.why: Room 2 (one box) gets 1 new box and Room 3 (none) gets 2, for 3 boxes. Rooms 1 and 4 need nothing. Only restocked rooms are logged: Rooms 2 and 3, so 2 rooms.

whyNot.1: This gives Room 3 one box; rooms with no boxes get two.
whyNot.2: The log records rooms you restock, not every room you check.
whyNot.3: Room 4 has two boxes, which matches neither restocking rule, so it gets none.

reteach.title: Directions are like turn-by-turn navigation
reteach.question: A navigation app says: 'In 500 feet, turn left. Then keep right at the fork, unless the bridge is closed; if it is, take the next exit.' What happens if you skip a turn or ignore the 'unless'?

blocks.h: Each instruction starts from where you are
blocks.body: Every navigation instruction assumes you followed the one before. Miss the left turn and 'keep right at the fork' leads somewhere else entirely. Ignore 'unless the bridge is closed' and you drive into a barrier. Written directions on the TEAS work the same way: each step builds on the last, and the condition words decide which road you take.

blocks.text: A real turn from later in the route is still the wrong answer to 'What next?' Answer the step the question asks for.

explain.body: Read all the steps first, then find exactly where the person is. The next step is the one immediately after, not a later step and not one already done.

test.q:
Read the directions.

1. Fill the kettle with cold water.
2. Boil the water, then let it cool for 2 minutes.
3. Pour the water over the tea bag.
4. Steep for 4 minutes, then remove the bag.

Nadia has just boiled the water. What should she do next?
options: Let the water cool for 2 minutes
Pour the hot water over the tea bag
Steep the tea for 4 minutes
Fill the kettle with cold water
test.why: Step 2 has two parts: boil, then cool for 2 minutes. Having boiled the water, Nadia lets it cool next.

whyNot.1: Pouring is step 3; it comes after the 2-minute cooling.
whyNot.3: Filling the kettle was step 1, already done.

explain.body: A conditional step splits the directions into branches. Decide which condition is true for the person in the question, then follow that branch only.

test.q:
Read the directions.

If the printer's status light is green, load the paper and press PRINT. If the light is orange, open the front panel and remove any jammed paper. If the light is off, check the power cable.

The light is orange. What should be done first?
options: Open the printer's front panel
Load the paper and press PRINT
Check the printer's power cable
Remove the paper from the tray
test.why: An orange light sends you to the second branch, which begins by opening the front panel.

whyNot.1: This branch is for a green light.
whyNot.2: Checking the cable is for a light that is off.
whyNot.3: The orange branch says to remove jammed paper after opening the panel, not to empty the tray.

explain.body: Unless = if not. Except = all but the named item. Only if = required condition. Also watch boundaries: 'more than 5' does not include 5; 'at or after' does include the time named.

test.q:
Read the policy.

Employees may wear sneakers on any shift unless they are working in the operating suite. Name badges must be worn on every shift.

Which employee is following the policy?
options: A nurse wearing sneakers and a badge on the medical floor
A nurse wearing sneakers and no badge on the medical floor
A technician wearing sneakers and a badge in the operating suite
An aide wearing loafers and no badge in the operating suite
test.why: Sneakers are allowed outside the operating suite, and a badge is required on every shift. The nurse on the medical floor with sneakers and a badge meets both rules.

whyNot.1: Badges must be worn on every shift.
whyNot.2: The 'unless' bars sneakers in the operating suite.
whyNot.3: The loafers are fine, but every employee must wear a badge.

explain.body: To find a skipped step, list what the person did against the directions, step by step. To find an outcome, apply every step in order to the situation described.

test.q:
Read the directions.

1. Turn off the unit.
2. Remove the old filter.
3. Write today's date on the new filter's label.
4. Slide the new filter in with the arrow pointing up.
5. Turn the unit back on.

Eli turned off the unit, removed the old filter, slid in the new filter with the arrow pointing up and turned the unit on. Which step did he skip?
options: Step 2
Step 3
Step 4
Step 5
test.why: Matching Eli's actions to the list, he did steps 1, 2, 4 and 5. He never wrote the date on the new filter's label, which is step 3.

whyNot.0: He removed the old filter, which is step 2.
whyNot.2: He slid in the new filter with the arrow up, which is step 4.
whyNot.3: He turned the unit back on, which is step 5.
